articles.title: Terrorists take 13 people hostage in Bannu
articles.description: BANNU: Terrorists allegedly took 13 people hostage on Friday as they were moving to a safer location due to the ongoing tensions between a local peace committee, police and militants in the mountainous Hathikhel area of Wazir subdivision, local sources said. According to sources, the people were stopped while they were transporting their belongings in vehicles to leave the area. The hostages were identified as four brothers, Rehmanullah, Farmanullah, Laiq and Sadiq; Mir Ali, Mohammad Raziq, Azim Khan and three brothers, including Sameen, Hamidullah and Rakhidullah. Three other individuals could not be identified. Police have not issued an official statement regarding the incident. However, police sources confirmed the incident. Meanwhile, a photograph purportedly showing the alleged hostages has also circulated on social media. The photograph also appears to show Nasir alias Gidarh, a local commander of the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan. The photograph and the identities of those shown in it could not be independently verified. Local sources said terrorists were allegedly trying to prevent residents from leaving the area and had imposed certain restrictions on those seeking to relocate. According to the sources, some families who failed to comply with the conditions allegedly had their houses demolished. These claims, however, could not be officially confirmed. The deteriorating security situation in Hathikhel and adjoining mountainous areas has continued to cause difficulties for residents, with several families reportedly moving to safer locations. Published in Dawn, September 27th, 2026

articles.title: Texas city council candidate charged with riot participation after ICE shooting protest
articles.description: AUSTIN, Texas (AP) — A Texas city council candidate was arrested Saturday morning on a misdemeanor charge for “riot participation," a week after he was part of a protest against the shooting of a Venezuelan man by a federal immigration officer. Public jail records do not specify the date of Misael Ramos' alleged rioting, but Ramos' attorney said that his client was accused of “engaging in a riot on the 20th of September," the day of the protests over the shooting of Wilber Rafael Garces Perez in Austin. Ramos denies any wrongdoing and will contest the charge, his campaign said in a news release. “I didn't see any riots,” said Ramos' attorney, Edmund Skip Davis. “I saw people out there chanting and protesting.” The arresting agency didn't immediately respond to questions from The Associated Press, and the details of the allegations against Ramos aren't yet clear. Ramos, a member of the Democratic Socialists of America, is running for city council in Austin. Ramos was released during a news conference outside the county jail Saturday, with the crowd erupting in cheers. Ramos thanked those for being there, saying it was “one of the craziest mornings I have had in a long time.” He spoke of his surprise arrest and against federal immigration raids in the community. “When we fight,” he said, to which those gathered replied, “we win!” Garces Perez was shot and then taken to a detention center after an encounter with an immigration officer. An attorney for Garces Perez has said he was an asylum seeker and had a valid work permit. Some Democrats have criticized the shooting, and the encounter has sparked protests in Austin, including a gathering outside the Texas Capitol on Monday night. “Like the hundreds of Austinites who were shocked to hear news that an ICE officer shot someone in the back, Misael quickly joined people at the scene of the incident to offer his condemnation of the incident and show solidarity by holding the line in the protest, chanting, and amplifying the incident through campaign channels,” Ramos' campaign manager, Jeffrey Clemmons, said in a statement provided to AP. Kristen Dark, a spokeswoman for the Travis County Sheriff's Office, confirmed in an email that Ramos was booked into the agency's custody around 9:30 Saturday morning on a charge of participating in a riot. Dark said additional details would have to come from the Texas Department of Public Safety, which conducted the arrest. The agency didn't immediately respond to calls or emails from the AP. Garces Perez was making a DoorDash delivery Sunday afternoon when ICE officers in an unmarked truck sideswiped his car twice, his attorney Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch has said. He was shot and taken to a hospital, then released into ICE custody with a bullet still in his back, she said. ICE and DHS haven’t said what led to the shooting beyond that Garces Perez was “the subject of a targeted vehicle stop.” This article originally appeared on Associated Press at https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/articles/texas-city-council-candidate-protested-213303799.html

articles.title: Gottmik arrested for DUI, crashed into multiple parked cars
articles.description: Gottmik is in trouble with the law. Prior to making comments on the future of drag at Revry's King of Drag premiere in West Hollywood last weekend, TMZ is now reporting that the Drag Race finalist was arrested for DUI . The news site claims that law enforcement was contacted around 4:50 PM on Wednesday, Sept. 16. Burbank Police officers responded to a traffic collision that involved a black Porsche and multiple parked vehicles. Allegedly, the driver of the Porsche collided with a parked Toyota Camry, which eventually hit two additional vehicles. 30-year-old Gottmik, whose real name is Kade Gottlieb, serves as the Porsche's sole occupant. According to police, the driver 'displayed objective signs and symptoms of alcohol intoxication' and was arrested for DUI. He was released the next day on Thursday, Sept. 17. Drag Race alum were quick to condemn Gottmik's arrest on social media. Season 18 contestant Briar Blush said, 'Economy so bad Gottmik didn’t wanna pay for an uber.' Season 14 finalist Daya Betty also chimed in on X by asking the question, 'Girl you can’t afford a ride share?' This isn't the first controversy for Gottmik in recent months. In January 2026, he faced backlash for attending and posing for photos at Marilyn Manson's birthday celebration alongside Violet Chachki. Gottmik has never publicly apologized or released an official statement regarding these situations.

articles.title: Man fatally shot during car chase in Grand Crossing
articles.description: A man was shot to death during a car chase Friday night in Grand Crossing on the South Side. The man, 26, was standing near his vehicle outside of a business in the 7500 block of South Cottage Grove Avenue when another vehicle drove by and someone from inside pointed a gun at him around 7 p.m., Chicago police said. The man got in his vehicle and drove away while the other vehicle followed him. The people inside the vehicle began shooting at him while in traffic, police said. The man was struck in the back and knee and hit a pole in the 7400 block of South Cottage Grove Avenue. He was taken to the University of Chicago Medical Center where he was pronounced dead, police said. His name hasn't been released. No arrests were made.
